messages:
incident-bot: !!! PAGE: GPU Capacity Exhaustion (us-west-2) — autoscaler failing to add nodes. Priority: P1. PD escalation to oncall.
maria (oncall): I'm on it. Paging rotation accepted. grabbing runbook -> https://redwood.runbooks/gpu-autoscale
ops-bot: PagerDuty run: INC-4921 assigned to maria (oncall). Notify: #incidents, #eng-sre, #eng-runtime
maria (oncall): Quick summary: spike in queued inference jobs (~4.2k) reported by queue-proxy. Autoscaler logs show repeated failures to attach new GPU nodegroups. Error snippets coming.
aj (infra): seeing errors in autoscaler logs: "Failed to create ASG: AttachRolePolicy limit exceeded" and "LaunchTemplate not found for version 0" — looks like a mix of IAM permission denies and stale launch template refs.
sam (sre): paste of autoscaler tail:
```
E0315 14:40:02.123 autoscaler.go:312] scaleUp: unable to scale up: error creating nodegroup: CreateFleet: UnauthorizedOperation: You are not authorized to perform this operation
caused by: AttachRolePolicy: exceeded rate limit attaching InstanceProfile
```
maria (oncall): ops: can you confirm whether we hit instance profile attach rate limits? Any recent rotation or rollout that changed instance profiles?
aj (infra): we rolled a new launch template last night for the gpu-pool (lt-0a1b2c3d) but I don't think it's available in all AZs. Also our instance profile attach API has a per-account throughput cap — looks like a burst of node creations from a canary + scheduled scaleback tripped it.
devon (support): customers A and B (beta) are reporting timeouts / 502s via support queue. I have a note to prioritize their traffic if we can route.
jen (eng-runtime): queue-proxy shows increased backpressure and a metric spike: token-drop-rate up 18%. We can temporarily divert non-critical requests to CPU pool or degrade to smaller model.
maria (oncall): immediate mitigations: 1) enable dedicated burst pool (if possible) 2) temporarily route low-priority traffic to CPU nodes 3) attempt manual nodegroup creation in one AZ to unblock queue. Any objections?
sam (sre): I'll try manual ASG create using existing launch template version that worked. Command:
```
aws autoscaling create-auto-scaling-group --auto-scaling-group-name gpu-temp-az1 --launch-template LaunchTemplateId=lt-0a1b2c3d,Version=1 --min-size 0 --max-size 10 --desired-capacity 3 --vpc-zone-identifier "subnet-aaa"
```
aj (infra): caution: if the launch template references an AMI that was deprecated, nodes will fail kube join. I'll watch the kubelet logs.
ops-bot: Incident note: created incident channel thread at 1718001234. Tagged for follow-up postmortem.
maria (oncall): sam — status?
sam (sre): ASG create returned success in us-west-2a, but kube nodes are tainted with experimental taint: gpupool/orphaned=true:NoSchedule. The taint appears from a mutating admission hook expecting a different launch template metadata tag.
jen (eng-runtime): that admission hook was updated in deployment v2.3 to require label gpu-pool=redwood-gpu. If new nodes don't have the tag because launch template version mismatch, controller adds taint.
devon (support): can we remove the taint for now to accept pods onto the new nodes?
sam (sre): we can, but risk: nodes might not have correct GPU drivers if AMI mismatch. Checking `kubectl describe node` — drivers present on node-3 but older drivers on node-4.
```
kubectl describe node ip-10-0-4-112 | grep -i nvidia
  Capacity:
    nvidia.com/gpu: 1
  Conditions: Ready
```
maria (oncall): Risk tradeoff: allow limited scheduling onto nodes with older drivers for low-priority traffic only. Jen — can runtime degrade requests safely to smaller kernel if driver mismatch detected?
jen (eng-runtime): yes, we can set a nodeSelector for degraded pool. I'll push a quick policy to route non-critical models to cpu-fallback or gpu-legacy pool.
aj (infra): also working with AWS support on the AttachRole rate limit. They advised to batch attach operations and requested quota bump; ETA unknown.
ops-bot: AWS support ticket 789234 opened by aj. Update expected in 2h.
maria (oncall): temporary steps executed: 1) manual ASG in us-west-2a (3 nodes) 2) removed taint gpupool/orphaned from 2 nodes (kubectl taint nodes node-3 gpupool/orphaned:NoSchedule- ) 3) routing rules updated to send 70% of low-priority queue to CPU fallback. Monitoring.
devon (support): letting affected customers know: "We're mitigating the issue by routing low-priority requests away from the GPU pool and provisioning temporary nodes; you may see degraded throughput for a short window."
sam (sre): queue length dropping from 4200 -> 900 over 12 minutes after mitigations. Error rate on hosted API for GPU models down from 12% -> 3%.
jen (eng-runtime): creating a guard: runtime will check launch-template-id label and auto-assign fallback pool if label mismatch. I'll open PR for reconciler.
aj (infra): follow-ups: ensure launch template versioning pipeline doesn't leave orphan LT refs, and change instance profile attach logic to retry/batch. Also add probe to detect attach rate limit near threshold.
maria (oncall): incident status: mitigated (read: customer impact reduced). Handing off to aj for infra remediation and to jen for runtime fix. I'll keep this channel open for coordination. PD: keep oncall rotated until ticket resolved.
ops-bot: Incident TIMELINE note appended. Please add any additional follow-ups.
maria (oncall): postmortem owners: aj (infra), jen (runtime). I'll schedule a 1-hour followup tomorrow. Thanks team. :heart:
